# Colleyville Chiropractic | CVC Spine

> Chiropractic clinic in Colleyville, Texas, serving the community since 1999. Chiropractic care, shockwave therapy, the NeuroPath neuropathy program, functional rehab, massage and recovery therapies for kids, athletes, expecting moms, seniors and everyone in between. In-network with Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas. Bilingual (English and Spanish).

- Address: 1001 Glade Rd, Suite 120, Colleyville, TX 76034
- Phone (call or text): (817) 420-7696
- Hours: Monday and Wednesday 9am to 6pm, Tuesday 2pm to 6pm, Thursday by appointment, Friday closed, Saturday 9am to 12pm, Sunday closed
- Booking: https://colleyvillechiropractic.janeapp.com/
- Chiropractor: Dr. Jon "Rudy" Urrutia, DC. Bachelor's degree and Doctor of Chiropractic from Parker University (2022), Advanced Activator certified, 10 years active duty U.S. Coast Guard
- New patient special: $47. New patient exam $120. Follow-up visit $60 ($45 member).
- Memberships: CVC Care $49/year, CVC Wellness $89/month, CVC Complete $169/month. Wellness and Complete include 2 recovery therapies a month (cupping, vibration plate or myofascial release).
- Online programs: https://resethybridrecovery.com/

## Services
- [Chiropractic Care](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/services/): A chiropractic adjustment is a quick, controlled force applied to a joint that isn't moving well, most often in the spine. It can reduce pain and muscle guarding and restore motion. The pop you may hear is gas releasing from the joint, not bones cracking.
- [Shockwave Therapy](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/shockwavetherapy/): Shockwave therapy, also called ESWT, uses a handpiece to deliver acoustic pressure waves into a painful tendon or soft tissue. The controlled stimulation increases blood flow and triggers a healing response in tissue that has stopped healing on its own. A typical plan is 5 to 10 sessions, once a week.
- [NeuroPath](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/neuropath/): NeuroPath is our program for peripheral neuropathy symptoms like numbness, tingling, burning and poor balance in the feet and hands. It starts with sensation, balance and circulation testing, then combines in-office visits, daily home light therapy and nerve stimulation, nutrition support and balance training, with re-testing to track change.
- [Functional Rehab](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/functionalrehab/): Functional rehab is coached, progressive exercise that rebuilds the strength, mobility and control your body needs for daily life and sport. Each program is matched to what you can't do right now and progressed visit by visit, not handed out as a generic sheet.
- [Massage Therapy](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/massagetherapy/): Massage therapy is hands-on work on muscles and connective tissue to ease tension, reduce soreness and help you recover. Sessions are tailored to your goal that day, from focused deep tissue work on a stubborn area to full-body relaxation.
- [Gut Health and Weight Management](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/guthealth/): Our gut health program is a personalized plan for nutrition, digestion and weight management, with regular check-ins to track progress. It focuses on habits you can keep instead of crash diets.
- [Cupping Therapy](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/cupping-therapy/): Cupping therapy uses cups that create gentle suction to lift the skin and underlying tissue. This decompresses tight muscle and draws blood flow to the area to ease tension and support recovery. The round marks it leaves are normal, painless and fade within about a week.
- [Myofascial Release](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/myofascial-release/): Myofascial release is sustained, targeted pressure and stretching of muscle and fascia, the connective tissue layer around muscle. It releases tight, restricted areas and improves how tissue glides, which often makes movement noticeably easier.
- [Red Light Therapy](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/red-light-therapy/): Red light therapy, or photobiomodulation, uses red and near-infrared light that your cells absorb. It may boost local energy production, support tissue repair and reduce inflammatory signaling. It doesn't damage skin the way UV does, and most people feel only gentle warmth.
- [Electrical Stimulation](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/electrical-stimulation/): Electrical stimulation, often called e-stim or TENS, uses soft adhesive pads to deliver a comfortable tingling current. It helps interrupt pain signals and relax muscle that has tightened up to guard an injury. It's included as one of your therapies with each chiropractic visit.
- [Therapeutic Ultrasound](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/therapeutic-ultrasound/): Therapeutic ultrasound uses a wand that glides over the skin with gel, sending sound waves that warm muscle and soft tissue below the surface. It's used to ease stiffness and prepare tissue for stretching and exercise, and it's included as one of your therapies with each chiropractic visit.
- [Pediatric Chiropractic](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/pediatric-chiropractic/): Pediatric chiropractic is chiropractic care adapted for children and teens, using gentle, low-force techniques like the Activator instrument and much lighter pressure than adult care. We focus on musculoskeletal issues like posture, sports strains and back or neck pain, and we refer to your pediatrician when something needs medical care.
- [Prenatal Chiropractic](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/prenatal-chiropractic/): Prenatal chiropractic is chiropractic care adapted for pregnancy. As your body changes, your posture, pelvis and low back take on new load. We use pregnancy-friendly positioning and gentler techniques to ease back, hip and pelvic pain, alongside simple exercises that help you stay comfortable and active.
- [Sports Chiropractic](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/sports-chiropractic/): Sports chiropractic combines adjustments, soft-tissue work, shockwave and progressive rehab to treat athletic injuries and get you back to training. We find what's driving the problem, which is often not where it hurts, then rebuild strength, power and control before you return.
- [Senior Chiropractic Care](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/senior-chiropractic/): Chiropractic care for seniors uses gentle, low-force techniques and adjusted pressure to ease back pain, stiffness and arthritis-related aches. We pair it with balance and strength work, because staying strong is one of the best ways to stay independent and reduce fall risk.
- [Diabetic Neuropathy](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/diabetic-neuropathy/): Diabetic peripheral neuropathy is nerve damage caused by high blood sugar over time. It usually starts in the toes and feet and moves upward, causing numbness, tingling, burning or sharp pain, and it can make balance worse and injuries easier to miss.
- [Chemotherapy-Induced Neuropathy](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/chemo-neuropathy/): Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is nerve damage caused by certain cancer drugs. It often affects both the hands and feet, causing numbness, tingling, burning or trouble with fine tasks like buttoning a shirt, and it can last months or years after treatment ends.
- [Numbness + Tingling in Feet](https://www.colleyvillechiropractic.com/numb-feet/): Numbness, tingling or burning in the feet usually comes from irritated or damaged nerves. The two most common sources are peripheral neuropathy, where the small nerves in the feet are affected, and a pinched nerve in the lower back, like sciatica or spinal stenosis. Age, vitamin B12 deficiency, alcohol, thyroid problems and some medications can also play a role.
